title: Nova SupplyChain intermittent load profile analysis
content:
Executive summary:

This note captures the benchmark and analysis we ran for Nova SupplyChain's POC to validate performance and cost under intermittent, bursty traffic typical of their shipment tracking APIs. The goal was to recreate production-like inter-arrival times (long quiet periods with short micro-bursts) and evaluate tail latency, cold-start behavior, KV cache effectiveness, and per-token cost across three model variants and two deployment configurations (hosted burstable vs dedicated pinned pool).

Objectives:
- Measure p50/p95/p99 generation latency for short prompts (avg 60 tokens output) at realistic burst sizes.
- Quantify cold-start penalty for scale-to-zero worker pools and for auto-burst paths.
- Compute estimated cost per 1M output tokens under observed throughput and compare Hosted vs Dedicated.
- Evaluate KV cache hit rate and impact on token-level latency/cost for repeated prefixes (shipment ID lookups).

Test matrix (high level):
- Models: open-7b-fp16 (baseline), open-7b-int8 (quantized), redwood-chat-4k (larger, slower but higher quality)
- Deployment modes: Hosted API (burstable, scale-to-zero enabled) and Dedicated pool (4x A10x GPUs pinned)
- Batching windows: 0ms (no batching), 8ms, 20ms
- Concurrency profiles: steady 10 qps, intermittent baseline (5s quiet, 2s burst at 100 qps), extreme microburst (1s at 500 qps every 30s)
- KV cache config: enabled (prefix-only 5k entries) vs disabled

Environment and test harness:
- Tests executed 2028-09-14 to 2028-09-19 from our EU region agents to match Nova's primary users.
- Prompts synthesized from anonymized shipment tracking dialogues (avg prompt tokens 30, expected output 45–75 tokens).
- Load generation via k6 scripts with randomized jitter to avoid perfectly aligned bursts.
- Instrumentation: per-request timestamping, route trace ids; metrics gathered from Redwood Console + local Prometheus scrape for more frequent samples.

Key results (selected highlights):
- Baseline steady 10 qps (open-7b-fp16, dedicated pool): p50=42ms, p95=88ms, p99=210ms; throughput sustained: 3200 tokens/s per GPU.
- Intermittent burst (open-7b-fp16, hosted burstable): first-burst cold-start median penalty = +820ms (p95 +2200ms). Subsequent bursts within 30s showed warm pools and p95 within 120–260ms.
- Quantized model (open-7b-int8, dedicated): p50=36ms, p95=72ms, p99=165ms; quality delta small for Nova prompts but hallucination risk increased on longer, multi-turn follow-ups.
- Larger model (redwood-chat-4k, dedicated): p50=96ms, p95=210ms, p99=480ms; higher cost but better slot-filling accuracy for ambiguous tracking messages.
- Batching tradeoffs: 8ms window reduced token cost by ~12% with negligible p50 increase (~+6ms), 20ms gave ~22% cost savings but p95 degraded by +45–70ms in tight bursts.
- KV cache: for repeated shipment prefixes (20% of requests), enabling cache lowered p95 by ~28% and reduced total token execution by ~14% in the workload run. Cache hit rate in experiments: 68% on repeated-prefix subset, overall effective hit ~14% due to many unique shipments.

Cost estimates (rough):
- Hosted (burstable, mixed 70% open-7b-fp16, 30% redwood-chat-4k): estimated $78 per 1M output tokens (includes burst overhead and scale-to-zero spin cost amortized across bursts).
- Dedicated (4x A10x pinned, same mix): estimated $42 per 1M output tokens (steady utilization assumptions), excluding reserved contract amortization.
- Quantized path reduces model execution cost ~22% relative to fp16 in our microbench environment (not counting quality tradeoffs).

Observed failure modes and risks:
- Cold-start variance: We saw large variance in cold-start times depending on concurrent control plane load in Hosted region; some warmups completed in 400ms, others exceeded 3s. This is the primary risk for tail-latency-sensitive endpoints.
- Microburst queuing: Very short, high-QPS spikes (500 qps, 1s) cause transient request queuing and CPU-side serialization on the request router—elevates p99 by up to 2.5x. SRE notes point to router thread pool tunables that partially mitigate this.
- Cache effectiveness limited by cardinality: Shipment IDs are high-cardinality; KV cache helps where clients send multiple follow-ups for same ID within short window, but global hit rate remains modest without client-side sticky routing or request coalescing.

Recommendations (prioritized):
1) Short term (for POC staging with customer):
   - Use Dedicated pool for production-like baselines when negotiating SLAs with Nova; provides predictable tail latency.
   - Enable open-7b-int8 as default to reduce unit cost; run small-scale quality gating for edge-case dialogues (we can route flagged messages to redwood-chat-4k).
   - Tune batching window to 8ms in Hosted for a balance of cost and latency during bursts; disable 20ms unless cost savings are required and tail-latency can be tolerated.
   - Add client-side sticky routing for session-bound requests so KV cache hit rate increases (recommend 60s stickiness).

2) Medium term (customer ops):
   - Implement request coalescing at the edge for repeated shipment ID lookups arriving within 200ms; we estimate ~10–15% token savings and reduced backend spikes.
   - Explore pre-warming strategies for expected scheduled bursts (e.g., nightly batch reports) via scheduled keep-alive pings to reduce cold-start variance.

3) Long term (platform):
   - Improve router autoscaling configuration for microburst throughput; add adaptive token-bucket shaping on ingress to protect model pools.
   - Investigate lightweight on-device prefix-caching at CDN/edge to reduce origin calls for extremely high-cardinality but read-heavy patterns.

Action items / follow-ups:
- Solutions eng to produce a short test harness (k6+configs) for Nova so they can replay production traces locally (owner: Ethan Ross, due 2028-09-25).
- Work with SRE to prototype router thread and connection pool tunables that reduce microburst queuing (owner: Liam O'Connor, due 2028-09-28).
- Run a 48-hour continuous mix test on Dedicated with client sticky routing enabled to validate real-world cache improvement (owner: Maya Chen, due 2028-10-05).

Appendix: raw numbers (selected runs)
- Dedicated | open-7b-fp16 | steady 10 qps | batch 0ms: p50 42ms, p95 88ms, p99 210ms, tokens/s/GPU 3200
- Hosted | open-7b-fp16 | intermittent burst (first burst): p50 120ms, p95 980ms, p99 2.4s (cold starts present)
- Dedicated | open-7b-int8 | intermittent burst warm: p50 38ms, p95 75ms, p99 170ms
- Dedicated | redwood-chat-4k | steady 10 qps: p50 96ms, p95 210ms, p99 480ms
- KV enabled run (dedicated, mixed workload): overall cache hit 14%, repeated-prefix p95 down 28%

Notes to reviewers:
- These numbers are test-harness outputs and include synthetic prompt mixes; actual customer traffic will vary. Quality impact from quantization needs product sign-off for Nova's acceptance tests—we recommend an A/B of 10k customer-like dialogues before finalizing default model.
- Linked artifacts above contain the k6 scenario and the JIRA ticket to track router tuning changes.

Raw logs and scripts location:
- github.com/redwood-inference/nova-poc-configs (see /bench/k6 and /bench/collectors)

If anything looks off or you want a deeper breakdown (per-route latency histograms, GPU-side profiler traces), ping me and we can add targeted slices.

-- Sofia
